title: The Lake at Veldes: the Dyer, the Atmospheric Cure, and the Sun Cult of Ascona
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Dye Works on the Aare

stops.name: Wangen an der Aare, the fourth of ten children
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by de.wikipedia and en.wikipedia
stops.campa: On the thirteenth of February a fourth child is born to a dye-works family on the Aare, in a Bernese market town under a covered wooden bridge. Nine other children come before and after him; the house lives by the vats, by indigo and mordant and the long boiling of cloth. Arnold Rikli grows up in a trade that turns water into color by chemistry, and he will spend the second half of his life arguing that water is the least of the elements. The dye works pays for his childhood and, in time, nearly kills him.
suggested_refs: The Rikli family dye works at Wangen an der Aare, Canton Bern

stops.name: Wangen an der Aare, the apprenticeship in his father's vats
stops.date_confidence: inferred: de.wikipedia places him in the parental dye works 'im zwanzigsten Lebensjahr', about 1842 or 1843, and has him leave for Carinthia in 1845; no month or day is recorded, so the date defaults to 01-01
stops.campa: In his twentieth year he is set to work in the family dye house and completes his apprenticeship as a dyer. The craft is exacting and the air is not: arsenic greens, chrome yellows, the vapors of hot mordant standing in a closed shed. He learns the whole trade and marries at twenty-one. Nothing in the training suggests a physician; everything in the working conditions prepares the patient he is about to become. The sons of the house are already looking south, where cloth is cheap to finish and land is cheaper.
suggested_refs: Swiss dyeing practice of the 1840s: mordants, arsenical greens, workshop ventilation

stops.name: Seebach bei Seeboden, the brothers' dyeing works
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; month and day unrecorded. The commodity is contested between sources, see campa. Seebach is an Ortschaft of the municipality Seeboden am Millstätter See, about five kilometres from Spittal an der Drau, so the two place-names in the literature are one place
stops.campa: Arnold, Karl and Rudolf Rikli leave Bern for Carinthia and set up a dyeing works at Seebach on the Millstätter See, five kilometres from Spittal an der Drau. The German account calls it a yarn-dyeing business; the English and Slovene accounts call it a leather-dyeing factory. The place is one place and the brothers are the same three; the sources simply do not agree on what went into the vats. They prosper for some years beside a lake in an Alpine valley, and the vats go on breathing at them.
suggested_refs: Seebach, Ortschaft of Seeboden am Millstätter See, Carinthia

segments.name: The Poisoned Trade and the First Lake

stops.name: Seebach, the trade turns on the dyer
stops.date_confidence: undated: the sources give no year for the onset of his illness, only that it precedes the journey to Veldes in 1852. 1850 is a placeholder inside that span, not an attested date
stops.campa: Rikli falls seriously ill and lays the blame on the chemicals of his own trade. The sources give no diagnosis and no date, only the sequence: a dyer breathes his workshop for years and then cannot go on. The medicine available to him offers drugs and mineral water. He begins instead to think about air, and about the light on the water outside the shed, and about the possibility that the cure is not a thing to be swallowed. From here his life turns on one conviction and never turns back.
suggested_refs: Occupational disease in nineteenth-century dyeing: no diagnosis survives for Rikli's own case

stops.name: Veldes, the first arrival at the lake
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by en.wikipedia, citing Berner Zeitung, 29 May 2023, and by sl.wikipedia; de.wikipedia's Rikli article does not carry the 1852 first visit. Month and day unrecorded
stops.campa: He comes for the first time to Veldes in Carniola, a lake under the Karawanken with an island church in the middle of it and a castle on the cliff above. He walks, he bathes, he sleeps in the open, and he gets better. The recovery is his own and it is the only clinical trial he will ever fully trust. Veldes at this date is a village of fishermen and boatmen with no cure trade at all. Within fifty years it will be one of the resorts of the empire, and the reason will be the sick dyer walking its shore.
suggested_refs: Veldes (Bled) before the cure trade: fishing village, island church, cliff castle

stops.name: Veldes, the family moves for good
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by de.wikipedia and en.wikipedia; month and day unrecorded
stops.campa: Recovered, Rikli moves his wife and children out of Carinthia and settles them permanently at Veldes. He is thirty-one and has no medical degree, no license, and no training beyond what his own body taught him in two summers on a lake. Slovene, German and Italian meet in this corner of the monarchy: the crown land is Carniola, the language of the village is Slovene, the language of the guests will be German. He begins looking at the western end of the water, where a spring called the Mallner Brunn comes out of the ground.
suggested_refs: The Mallner Brunn spring at the western end of Lake Bled

stops.name: Mallner Brunn, Veldes: the Naturheilanstalt opens
stops.date_confidence: 1855 per en.wikipedia, sl.wikipedia and Rikli's own first-person account in the 1905 French edition; de.wikipedia's 'Bled' article dates the founding of the Mallnerbrunn institute to 1858 and its 'Arnold Rikli' article implies 1854. The contradiction is left standing. Month and day unrecorded
stops.campa: At the spring called Mallner Brunn, on the north-western shore, Rikli opens the Naturheilanstalt Mallnerbrunn, a natural healing institute for the atmospheric cure. Patients come chiefly in summer. They rise early, walk barefoot in the wet grass, eat vegetarian food, bathe in the lake, and lie in the sun with as little on them as the century will permit. At the end of the sun bath he wraps them in a dry sheet, the maillot sec, to force the sweat the sun alone will not draw from every body.
stops.quote: Lors de l'inauguration de mon établissement de médecine naturelle à Veldes, en 1855, j'introduisis le maillot sec.
stops.quote_source: Arnold Rikli, Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil (Lausanne: Georges Bridel & Cie, 1905), ch. III, 'Souvenirs historiques', p. 35
suggested_refs: Naturheilanstalt Mallnerbrunn, Veldes, opened 1855 (1858 per de.wikipedia 'Bled')
sources: Arnold Rikli, Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil (Lausanne, 1905)

stops.name: Veldes, sun-bathing declared a treatment
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by de.wikipedia; June is a placeholder for the first cure season and is not a recorded month
stops.campa: The same year he makes his heliotherapy public: the sun bath is not a pleasure of the season but a prescription, with a dose and a duration. The claim offends the medical faculties and the parish at once, since it requires the patient to be uncovered in the open air in a Catholic crown land. Rikli answers with anatomy. Man is not a fish and not an amphibian; he stands upright in the air with his feet on the ground, and what falls on him from above is what he was built to receive.
stops.quote: On ne peut le considérer dans sa vraie nature que comme une créature de lumière et d'air. L'eau est à ses pieds!
stops.quote_source: Arnold Rikli, Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil, § 38 (Lausanne: Georges Bridel & Cie, 1905)
suggested_refs: Rikli's 1855 publication of the sun-bathing method
sources: Arnold Rikli, Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil (Lausanne, 1905)

stops.name: Veldes, bathing in the atmosphere instead of the water
stops.date_confidence: undated: the definition is quoted from the 1905 French edition and cannot be fixed to a year. 1860 is a placeholder inside the institute's first decade
stops.campa: Water cures are the fashion of the century: Priessnitz at Gräfenberg, Kneipp later in Bavaria, wet sheets and cold plunges and douches falling from a height. Rikli takes the whole apparatus and lifts it out of the water into the air. His own one-line answer to the question of what the atmospheric cure consists in is a joke with a doctrine inside it. The patient at Veldes is asked to do very little except be outdoors, uncovered, from morning, and to keep doing it for weeks together.
stops.quote: A ceux qui demanderont en quoi consiste la cure atmosphérique, nous répondrons simplement: A se baigner dans l'atmosphère au lieu de le faire dans l'eau!
stops.quote_source: Arnold Rikli, Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil, § 38 (Lausanne: Georges Bridel & Cie, 1905)
suggested_refs: The hydropathic establishments Rikli argued against: Gräfenberg, Wörishofen
sources: Arnold Rikli, Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil (Lausanne, 1905)

stops.name: Veldes, man as the highest terrestrial plant
stops.date_confidence: undated: doctrine quoted from the 1905 French edition; 1862 is a placeholder inside the institute's first decade
stops.campa: The metaphor at the centre of the system is botanical. Feet are roots, torso is trunk, head is crown; the human body is a plant that has learned to walk, and like any plant it lives on light. From this it follows that houses, clothes, shade and parasols are pathologies of civilization, each one a further layer between the crown and the sun. Rikli's patients spend their days undressed in a mountain valley doing what a plant does, which is to stand in the weather and take what comes.
stops.quote: L'homme doit être considéré comme la plante terrestre la plus développée; c'est pour son plus grand dommage qu'il s'isole de l'atmosphère comme il le fait par son habitation, sa manière de se vêtir, son goût pour l'ombre... et pour les parasols!
stops.quote_source: Arnold Rikli, Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil, § 38 (Lausanne: Georges Bridel & Cie, 1905)
suggested_refs: Rikli's botanical anatomy: feet as roots, torso as trunk, head as crown
sources: Arnold Rikli, Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil (Lausanne, 1905)

stops.name: Veldes, four years of light baths on his own body
stops.date_confidence: attested: Rikli dates the experiment 1865 to 1868 in his own text; month and day unrecorded
stops.campa: Before he will give the light bath to a paying guest, Rikli takes it himself every morning for four years, winter and summer, in the open air of a Julian Alpine valley. This is the difference between him and the physicians who dismiss him: he runs the trial on one subject and the subject is the doctor. At the end of the fourth year he judges the evidence sufficient and writes the light bath into the plan of the cure, beside the sun bath, the water, the walking and the vegetarian table.
stops.quote: Durant quatre années, de 1865 à 1868, je pratiquai les bains de lumière comme expérience de rafraîchissement, hiver et été, chaque matin, sur moi-même.
stops.quote_source: Arnold Rikli, Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil (Lausanne: Georges Bridel & Cie, 1905), ch. III, 'Souvenirs historiques', p. 35
suggested_refs: Rikli's four-year self-experiment with the light bath, 1865-1868
sources: Arnold Rikli, Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil (Lausanne, 1905)

stops.name: Veldes, persuading the guests out of bed
stops.date_confidence: inferred: Rikli places the introduction of the light bath after the fourth year of self-testing, therefore from 1869; no month recorded
stops.campa: The light bath is taken at first light, straight out of bed, and the paying guests of a nineteenth-century spa do not want it. They call it a specialist's hobby-horse. Rikli argues them into the meadow one at a time, half-convinced, and the practice takes hold only because the man who invented it has been doing it alone at dawn through four winters and does not appear to be joking. Within two generations the same practice, taken up by people who never heard his name, will look like a movement.
stops.quote: Que de paroles pour réussir à entraîner quelques-uns de mes hôtes...
stops.quote_source: Arnold Rikli, Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil (Lausanne: Georges Bridel & Cie, 1905), ch. III, 'Souvenirs historiques', p. 36
suggested_refs: Guest resistance to the dawn light bath, recorded in Rikli's 'Souvenirs historiques'
sources: Arnold Rikli, Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil (Lausanne, 1905)

stops.name: Ljubljana, the winter practice
stops.date_confidence: undated: de.wikipedia says only that he treated patients at Ljubljana during the winter months, ongoing from the 1850s. 1870 is a placeholder inside that span
stops.campa: Veldes empties when the snow comes and the sun bath is unusable for half the year. Rikli follows his patients down to the provincial capital and keeps a winter practice at Laibach, the town the Slovenes call Ljubljana, some fifty kilometres south-east of the lake. The cure adapts: less sun, more air, the same insistence on the open window and the walk before breakfast. The institute at Mallner Brunn is a summer machine, and its maker spends the cold half of every year as a travelling doctor.
suggested_refs: Rikli's winter consulting practice at Laibach/Ljubljana

stops.name: Trieste, the winter cure at the imperial port
stops.date_confidence: undated: de.wikipedia names Trieste as a winter station without years; 1875 is a placeholder. The coordinates are the atlas's canonical Trieste pin, inherited byte-identical from freud.journey.json and dannunzio.journey.json
stops.campa: The circuit reaches the sea. At Trieste, the empire's port on the Adriatic, Rikli winters and treats: the mildest station on his route, chosen for the same reason he chose Veldes in the first place, air a sick man can stand to breathe. It is a cosmopolitan Habsburg port that draws visitors and residents for every reason under the sun, from trade to medicine, and its winters are gentle enough to keep his barefoot, half-dressed regimen workable when the mountain lake freezes over. Rikli, in these years, is a Swiss dyer telling Austrians to open their windows.
suggested_refs: Trieste as winter station of the Rikli circuit; the atlas's shared Trieste pin
sources: dannunzio.journey.json, stop 'Over Trieste, the first flight of the poet-aviator'

stops.name: Gries bei Bozen, the third winter station
stops.date_confidence: undated: de.wikipedia names Gries near Bozen as a winter station without years; 1880 is a placeholder
stops.campa: The last of his winter stations is Gries, outside Bozen in the South Tyrol, already a fashionable Kurort where consumptive northerners come for mild air under the Dolomites. Rikli arrives into an established trade and works it on his own terms. Three winter towns and one summer lake: the whole geography of his working life fits inside the Austrian half of the monarchy. He never practices in the country he was born in. Switzerland will get him back only as a book, and only at the end.
suggested_refs: Gries bei Bozen as an Alpine Kurort of the 1870s and 1880s

stops.name: Veldes, the books begin to go out
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year: the earliest of the five Rikli originals held by the National and University Library of Slovenia is dated 1872; month unrecorded
stops.campa: From 1872 he publishes. Five of his own editions survive in a single collection, dated 1872, 1889, 1890 and 1894, with an undated offprint from a journal of hygiene and nature cure. The argument in all of them is one argument: the nervous system is the most perfected organic product of sunlight, and sunlight is therefore the food it was made for. He is not writing for physicians, who have refused him already. He is writing for the patients, who arrive at the lake each June having read him.
stops.quote: [La lumière solaire] sera donc toujours, en sa qualité de mère, sa nourriture la meilleure et la plus fortifiante.
stops.quote_source: Arnold Rikli, Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil, § 39 (Lausanne: Georges Bridel & Cie, 1905); the bracketed subject replaces the original pronoun 'Celle-ci', which refers back to sunlight in the preceding sentence
suggested_refs: The five Rikli originals, 1872-1894, National and University Library of Slovenia
sources: Arnold Rikli, Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil (Lausanne, 1905)

stops.name: Veldes, life is a molecular movement
stops.date_confidence: undated: the axioms are quoted from the 1905 French edition, itself translated from the eighth German edition of Die Grundlehren der Naturheilkunde. 1885 is a placeholder inside the publishing years
stops.campa: The system rests on four sentences of physics, or of something wearing the clothes of physics. Life is molecular movement. Force is the capacity of matter to move. Health is normal movement of matter, and disease is abnormal movement of matter. The rest of Rikli follows from this: if disease is bad motion, then the cure is whatever moves the body fastest and most cleanly, and the fastest thing that touches a human being is light. The lake, the meadow and the dry sheet are all consequences of an axiom.
stops.quote: La vie est un mouvement moléculaire. La force est la capacité qu'a la matière de se mouvoir. La santé est un mouvement normal de la matière. La maladie est un mouvement anormal de la matière.
stops.quote_source: Arnold Rikli, Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil, § 1 (Lausanne: Georges Bridel & Cie, 1905)
suggested_refs: Die Grundlehren der Naturheilkunde, 8th German edition, source of the 1905 translation
sources: Arnold Rikli, Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil (Lausanne, 1905)

stops.name: Veldes, the three elements ranked by speed
stops.date_confidence: undated: § 45 of the 1905 French edition; 1888 is a placeholder inside the publishing years
stops.campa: The slogan the resort still sells, water is good, air is better, light is best, has a technical parent inside the books. Rank the three elements by the speed of their molecular movement and the order comes out fixed: light first, then air, then water last of all. The maxim is the marketing and the ranking is the reason. His contemporaries selling cold water at Gräfenberg and Wörishofen have, on this arithmetic, picked the slowest of the three and built their establishments on it.
stops.quote: Du reste, c'est à proportion de la rapidité de leurs mouvements moléculaires que ces trois éléments sont importants pour le corps; or la lumière possède le plus rapide, puis vient l'air, puis enfin seulement l'eau.
stops.quote_source: Arnold Rikli, Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil, § 45 (Lausanne: Georges Bridel & Cie, 1905)
suggested_refs: The Slovene form of the maxim: 'Voda je dobra, še boljši je zrak, a najboljša je svetloba.'
sources: Arnold Rikli, Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil (Lausanne, 1905)

stops.name: Veldes, Hufeland's sentence borrowed
stops.date_confidence: undated: § 40 of the 1905 French edition quotes Hufeland's Macrobiotik, 6th ed., p. 87. 1890 is a placeholder inside the publishing years
stops.campa: Rikli did not invent the primacy of light and does not claim to. He quotes it from Christoph Wilhelm Hufeland, the Weimar physician who attended Goethe and Schiller and whose Macrobiotik taught a generation how to think about long life. Hufeland set light at the summit of the four heavenly gifts sixty years earlier and left it there as a sentence. Rikli builds on the sentence an institute, a daily regimen, a season, and eventually a town whose whole economy depends on its being true.
stops.quote: La lumière, la chaleur, l'air et l'eau, dons célestes, qu'on peut à bon droit dénommer les esprits protecteurs de la vie! Au faîte est la lumière, incontestablement le plus proche parent de la vie, et, par conséquent, d'une importance bien plus grande qu'on ne le pense en général.
stops.quote_source: Christoph Wilhelm Hufeland, Macrobiotik, 6th ed., p. 87, quoted by Arnold Rikli in Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil, § 40 (Lausanne: Georges Bridel & Cie, 1905)
suggested_refs: Christoph Wilhelm Hufeland, Makrobiotik oder Die Kunst das menschliche Leben zu verlängern
sources: Arnold Rikli, Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil (Lausanne, 1905)

stops.name: Veldes, the villa, the baths and the hospital
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by en.wikipedia; month unrecorded. en.wikipedia says only 'a villa and baths in the Swiss architectural style, along with a hospital featuring his own examination office', with no further detail
stops.campa: Forty years after the first season Rikli builds in stone and timber: a villa, baths, and a hospital with his own examination room, all in the Swiss architectural style he brought from the Aare. The Bernese chalet arrives on a Carniolan lake as the visible signature of the cure. Guests who have read the books now find a whole establishment waiting for them, and a village of fishermen has acquired an architecture imported wholesale from the valley where the dyer was born.
suggested_refs: The 1895 building campaign at Mallnerbrunn: villa, baths, hospital, Swiss style

stops.name: Veslaška promenada, the Kursalon
stops.date_confidence: undated: sl.wikipedia describes the villa as the Kursalon of the institute without giving a construction year. 1897 is a placeholder between the 1895 building campaign and the 1899 enlargement. The address, Veslaška promenada 12, is mapped in OpenStreetMap
stops.campa: The villa serves as the Kursalon, the social room of the cure, where guests on the same regimen meet between the morning light bath and the evening walk. It stands on the north-western shore at Veslaška promenada 12, and it is still standing. Slovenia lists it as a protected cultural monument. Everything else Rikli built at the lake is gone or absorbed into later hotels; this one building keeps his name at a street address, which is more than the institute itself managed.
suggested_refs: Riklijeva vila (the Kursalon), Veslaška promenada 12, Bled, protected cultural monument

stops.name: Straža, the paths of the cure
stops.date_confidence: undated: en.wikipedia records a path 'that led to Straža Hill' and sl.wikipedia confirms the walking routes, neither with a year. 1898 is a placeholder. Coordinates are the Straža summit per OpenStreetMap
stops.campa: Walking is half the treatment, and Rikli lays out routes above the lake for it. One climbs Straža, the wooded hill on the southern shore, up through the pines and back down to the water. Patients go up in the early morning with as little on them as decency permits, and come down to the bath with the sweat already raised. The hill carries a ski slope and a summer toboggan run now, worked in both directions by people who have never once heard the doctrine that first cut the path into it.
suggested_refs: The Straža hill path above Lake Bled, laid out for the Rikli cure

stops.name: Veldes, the larger swimming area
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by en.wikipedia, which says a larger swimming area with promenade was added in 1899; the wording is 'added', not 'replaced', so the fate of the 1895 baths is not stated. Month unrecorded
stops.campa: A larger swimming area with a promenade is added to the establishment. The cure has outgrown its buildings twice in five years. Veldes now has a season, a clientele drawn from German-speaking Europe, hotels going up around the water, and a founding doctor of seventy-six who still takes his light bath at dawn. In the summer of this same year three guests arrive who will carry the whole system over the Alps into Italian Switzerland, and not one of them comes to Rikli for that purpose.
suggested_refs: The 1899 enlargement of the bathing complex at Mallnerbrunn

segments.name: The Guests of 1899 and the Last Years

stops.name: Mallnerbrunn, Ida Hofmann and Henri Oedenkoven
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by de.wikipedia and en.wikipedia, 'Monte Verità'; month unrecorded. The sources differ on Hofmann's footing at the institute, see campa
stops.campa: Ida Hofmann, a music teacher of Bavarian family, comes to Bled because her father is gravely ill, and takes lodgings at the Naturheilanstalt Mallnerbrunn. Henri Oedenkoven, twenty-five, son of an Antwerp industrialist, is there as a patient taking the cure. The German account makes her a lodger and him a patient; the English account makes them both patients of a shared cure. Either way they meet inside Rikli's establishment, under Rikli's regimen, and they leave it together with a plan.
suggested_refs: de.wikipedia, 'Ida Hofmann': 'Sie selbst mietete sich in der nahe gelegenen Naturheilanstalt Mallnerbrunn ein'

stops.name: Mallnerbrunn, Karl Gräser under the Sun Doctor
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by de.wikipedia and en.wikipedia, 'Monte Verità'; June is a placeholder for the cure season. The nickname Sonnendoktor is [R], a secondary-source description of local usage rather than a quotation from any document
stops.campa: Karl Gräser, a former Austrian officer who has renounced money, uniform and cooked food, is taking the cure at Veldes in the same season. The village calls Rikli the Sonnendoktor, the Sun Doctor, and the word travels out with the guests. Gräser, Oedenkoven and Hofmann hold between them the entire kit of the coming century: vegetarianism, the uncovered body in open air, light as medicine, the reform of the body as the reform of everything else. They need a hill.
suggested_refs: Karl and Gustav Gräser, founders of the Monte Verità cooperative

stops.name: Monte Verità, Ascona: the hill bought as Monte Monescia
stops.date_confidence: attested to the autumn of 1900 by de.wikipedia, 'Monte Verità': the group met at Munich in October 1900 and bought land on Monte Monescia above Ascona that autumn; the name Monte Verità was adopted only in 1902. November is a placeholder inside the attested season. Coordinates are the atlas's canonical Monte Verità pin, inherited byte-identical from laban.journey.json
stops.campa: The guests of Bled meet again at Munich in October and buy a hill above Ascona on Lake Maggiore before the year is out. Monte Monescia, renamed Monte Verità in 1902, becomes a vegetarian cooperative whose members live in light-and-air huts, garden uncovered, refuse meat and alcohol and property, and take the sun as a sacrament. The regimen is Rikli's regimen moved four hundred kilometres west and stripped of its doctor. He is alive, seventy-seven, and no source records that anyone told him.
suggested_refs: The founding of the Monte Verità cooperative, autumn 1900, by Oedenkoven, Hofmann, Karl and Gustav Gräser
sources: laban.journey.json, stop 'Monte Verità, Ascona: arrival on the sacred hill'

stops.name: Vienna, the gold medal
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by en.wikipedia and sl.wikipedia; no month, and no source names the exhibition or its hall, so the coordinates are the city centre and stand in for an unlocated venue
stops.campa: At an international exposition of healing destinations held in the imperial capital, Bled takes a gold medal. The village that had no cure trade at all in 1852 is certified by Vienna as one of the empire's health resorts. Rikli is eighty. The prize goes to the town and not to him, which is the correct address: he made a place rather than a clinic, and the place is now large enough to collect its own honours while its founder is still alive to read about them.
suggested_refs: The 1903 Vienna international exposition for healing destinations (venue unidentified in reachable sources)

stops.name: Lausanne, the cure translated into French
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year: the Georges Bridel edition is dated 1905; month unrecorded. The translator is not credited in the volume
stops.campa: Georges Bridel of Lausanne brings out Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil, a French translation of the eighth German edition of the Grundlehren der Naturheilkunde. The dyer's son returns to Switzerland at eighty-two in the form of a book, in the third of his country's languages, printed two hundred kilometres from the Aare. The preface states the purpose without ornament: to teach the reader to think carefully and logically about his own condition, and to draw sensible conclusions from it.
stops.quote: Le but de cette brochure est d'indiquer d'une façon générale et claire l'esprit de la médecine naturelle et d'enseigner ainsi à penser, avec prudence et logique, à son propre état pour en tirer des conclusions sensées.
stops.quote_source: Arnold Rikli, Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil, Avant-propos (Lausanne: Georges Bridel & Cie, 1905), translated from the 8th German edition of Die Grundlehren der Naturheilkunde, translator uncredited
suggested_refs: Arnold Rikli, Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil (Lausanne: Georges Bridel & Cie, 1905)
sources: Arnold Rikli, Médecine naturelle et bains de soleil (Lausanne, 1905)

stops.name: Sankt Thomas, Carinthia: the death
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by de.wikipedia and en.wikipedia. de.wikipedia links the death place to the Wolfsberg district and Wikidata Q124423 gives place of death as Wolfsberg; coordinates are St. Thomas in the Katastralgemeinde St. Marein per OpenStreetMap. No source explains why he is in the Lavant valley, and Wikidata carries no place-of-burial statement at all
stops.campa: Arnold Rikli dies at Sankt Thomas in the Lavant valley of Carinthia, aged eighty-three, three hundred kilometres east of the lake he made. Nothing found says why he is there. Nothing found says where he is put into the ground. The man who spent fifty years arguing that the body is a plant and light is its food leaves no attested grave, and the standard biographies in three languages pass over the question in silence rather than answering it badly.
